name: Osborn R. Keith house (1808 Prairie Avenue), K01 frontage assembly

function.note: The 1911 Sanborn sheet 28 draws a three-storey-and-basement brick house ('3B') with a rear two-storey garage on the lot; a house of that kind on Prairie Avenue in 1904 is a residence. The T-1837 building register names it the Osborn R. Keith (later Stanley Field) residence, reported 1886 by Cobb & Frost; that register's evidence handles are not yet source records here, so the names ride in the record's name and aka, not in a cited attribute.

research_note: T-2266 — the first assembly built to the Prairie 1904 K01 metric component contract (data/components/prairie_1904/k01_contract.json, T-2265), beside the canonical Glessner asset. It is a SMALL PROOF, not the house: the street front, side and rear walls of the main range with their openings, the entry stoop and a hip roof, every part a K01 component with a stable id, a seed and metric UVs, and every dimension a reconstruction inside the contract's declared ranges. What the house actually looked like — the rock-faced Romanesque-classical front, the south curved bay, the north entrance loggia with Ionic columns, the pierced parapet (T-1837 FRONTAGE-REGISTER frontage-28-037, read from the Inland Architect plate of February 1888) — is owned by T-1882 and T-1883, the detached rear garage by T-1935; this assembly replaces none of that and is replaced by it. The north wall closes the Glessner courtyard 0.02 m south of Glessner's south face, the clearance the K01 measure needs to keep two assets' faces from coinciding (docs/LIBERTIES.md, T-2266). T-2499 (piece 1 of T-1882) began replacing it from the Inland Architect plate of February 1888: the hip, dormer and cresting gave way to a flat top behind a front parapet standing over Glessner's ridge, the floors were raised to the plate's courses, the south bow was stopped at floor 3 under a moulded cap, and the third storey was run flat across the front as an arcade of six lights. The north loggia and its stair are T-2500's; the lattice, pinnacles, diaper band, colonnettes, stone tone and fence are T-1883's. T-1883 replaces the remaining street-front kit proof with the approved 1888 photograph's pierced top, diaper, colonnettes, paired Ionic capitals, carved balcony and scrolled stair cheeks, granite courses and early stone boundary. Fine carving, the hidden roof, rear, exact colour and yard surfaces remain explicitly reconstructed.

documented_range.note: STANDING IN 1904 is what the scene needs, and it rests on the 1911 Sanborn sheet 28 carried back seven years, the same reading the Glessner record and the 1904 parcels make of it (the Glessner House correspondent reads no change on this sheet between 1904 and 1911). FROM: the T-1837 building register reports 1886 (Cobb & Frost); it is not a source record here, so the day is the 1st of January and the confidence inferred. TO: the register reports the loss in 1968; same footing, the year's last day.

position.symbolic_location: 1808 S. Prairie Avenue: west side of Prairie between 18th and 20th Streets, the lot directly south of the Glessner house, parcel prairie_1808 (data/street_grid/1904.json).
position.note: Placed in the Glessner record's own frame, so the two share one bearing and one building line exactly. The footprint origin (its SW corner) is Glessner-frame u 31.149, v -10.42: the front wall on Glessner's east face line (u 49.149, 14.7 ft behind the Prairie Avenue line — RECONSTRUCTED: Sanborn 1911 draws 1808 set back on a common line with its neighbour, and the sheet is not read here to the foot for this lot), and the north wall 0.02 m south of Glessner's south face (v 0), closing its courtyard as the sheet draws. The south wall then stands 1.1 m inside the parcel's south line at the street. Rotation -0.669 degrees is Glessner's, the 18th Street line's bearing less 90.

derivation.reason: The four derivation methods re-derive from the 1835 files; none reads the 1904 street grid or another record's frame. This position is the Glessner record's footprint origin moved by (u 31.149, v -10.42) metres in Glessner's own frame at its rotation (-0.669 degrees, clockwise from grid north), and the note carries both numbers so the sum can be recomputed by hand from data/structures/glessner_house.json.

footprint.note: The main range only, 18.0 m deep by 10.4 m across the front. RECONSTRUCTED: the 1911 sheet draws a brick house the width of most of its 38.1 ft lot, but its depth and side passage are not read here to a figure; 10.4 m leaves a 1.1 m passage on the south and 18.0 m is a Prairie Avenue town house of three bays. The detached rear garage the sheet also draws is T-1935's.

stories.note: '3B' on the 1911 Sanborn sheet 28: three storeys and a basement. Carried back to 1904 with the sheet.

construction.note: The 1911 sheet colours the house brick, and the T-1837 frontage register reads it 'brick with stone front'. The stone front is the register's reading of the 1888 plate, so the pairing is carried here as the sheet's brick plus a reconstructed stone street wall.

principal_floor_m.note: T-1883: The principal deck stands about 2.0 m above grade in the plate, read from the basement band and the stair. Replaces the 1.5 m kit proof retained by T-2499/T-2500 pending the boundary finish. The stair now ends behind the street line with no gate swing to obstruct it.

storey_heights_m.note: T-2499: Read off the Inland Architect plate of February 1888 (photograph c. 1887), the nearly square-on view of the front: its 10.4 m front spans about 455 px between the corner piers at the principal storey, about 43.8 px/m, and the camera stands low, so readings high on the front are a little short and are rounded up. Floor 2 stands at the string course under the second storey's sills (about 5.8 m over grade on the plate), set at 5.9 m; floor 3 at the bow's moulded cap (about 9.8 m), so the bow's two storeys end on it; the third storey carries the six-light arcade (about 10.6 to 12.7 m) and the deep diaper band over it (about 13.0 to 14.9 m) up to the moulded course under the parapet, about 5.3 m short, set at 5.4 m. The wall head stands at 15.2 m and the front parapet's top at about 16.5 m, over Glessner's ridge (15.5 m in glessner_house__as_built_1887.glb) as the plate and a18-gh-glessner-front-with-keith show it. The principal storey is 4.4 m because the principal floor stays at its reconstructed 1.5 m where the plate reads about 2.0 m (principal_floor_m says why); the plate's own principal storey is about 3.8 m. Before T-2499 these were [4.0, 3.6, 3.3], a reconstruction under a hip roof whose eave stood near Glessner's. T-1883 raises the principal deck to 2.0 m and reduces its storey to 3.9 m; the accepted second/third floors and wall head remain at 5.9, 9.8 and 15.2 m.

wall_thickness_front_m.note: The stone street wall at the top of the contract's masonry range [0.23, 0.45]; it sets the reveal depth of every front opening.

wall_thickness_side_m.note: Common brick, a 13-inch wall, inside the masonry range; the Sanborn sheet prints no wall thickness for this lot.

service_wall_brick.note: The 1911 Sanborn sheet colours the house brick and the T-1837 register asks for 'Common-brick side and rear ranges'; the fabric, bond, heads, string course and grime are the K03 library's common buff brick in common bond (a header course every sixth, 9 mm weathered lime joints), laid with two rowlock rings on segmental heads (soldier flat heads under the eave), a projecting string course at the second floor and soot and damp masks, with no photograph of 1808's side or rear read (liberty L-k03-1808-service-brick-2291, T-2291).

street_front_trim.note: The street front's carved trim, from the K09 carved-trim kit (T-2309, data/components/prairie_1904/k09_trim.json): the principal-floor windows in the kit's restrained surround (an architrave, and a cornice hood on scrolled consoles) over a bounded foliate apron panel; the second floor's windows under the cornice hood alone; the third floor's keeping K01's flat lintel, so the trim lightens as the front rises. RECONSTRUCTED: the T-1837 register reads 'Romanesque-classical stone front' and an Ionic-columned entrance loggia off the 1888 Inland Architect plate, but that plate is not a source record here and no photograph of 1808's carving has been read, so every form, motif and placement is the kit's generic one (liberty L-k09-1808-trim-2310, T-2310). Glessner's documented carving is its own and is not drawn from this kit. T-2500: the K09 ring of voussoirs on colonnettes that stood over the door is gone: the door now stands at the back of the north loggia the 1888 plate draws, under its ceiling 3.45 m over the floor, which the ring's 3.8 m crown would have passed through, and the plate shows nothing of the door in the loggia's shadow (entrance_kit).

clear_of.note: Glessner's south gable stands against the party wall here: read off glessner_house__as_built_1887.glb in this frame, its mass within 0.40 m of the wall rises above the brackets' feet (11.34 m) from u 11.4 to u 16.2 (s 1.8 to 6.6), to 14.70 m at u 13.5. No bracket stands in it; the bed moulding, like the K05 eave above it, runs on inside the gable.

wall_head.note: T-2499: the moulded stone course the plate draws between the diaper band and the parapet, from the K10 kit's moulded_stone cornice (data/components/prairie_1904/k10_cornices.json), projecting 0.35 m (eave_overhang_m). The flat top carries no cresting and no dormer, so both are gone with the hip (T-2316's bracketed timber cornice and T-2326's pedimented dormer were on that reconstructed roof). The clear_of span stays: Glessner's south gable against the party wall. Shape only; its profile and carving are T-1883's.

roof_form.note: T-2499: the plate, the mid-1950s and 1967 photographs and the owner's photograph all show a flat top: no roof slope or dormer shows from the street over the parapet. Built as K01's k01.roof.flat (T-2350), K05's flat_parapet deck falling to the rear wall behind level parapets on the side walls and a blocking course over the front. What covers the deck nobody sees from the street and is reconstructed (roof_covering). Before T-2499 the record carried a reconstructed hip with a gabled dormer, an Italianate top the owner reported against the pictures on 2026-10-13. The pierced lattice, the pinnacles and the diaper work are T-1883's finish on these shapes.

roof_pitch_deg.note: T-2499: the deck's fall to the rear wall, K05's flat_parapet 2 degrees, inside the contract's flat range. Unseen from the street; nothing reads it.

eave_overhang_m.note: T-2499: the stone course under the parapet projects 0.35 m, the least that clears the K10 moulded_stone section's 0.32 m projection inside the fascia (k10_frontage), and inside a K01 flat roof's 0.3-1.0 m street cornice: the plate draws a thin moulded course over the diaper band, not a deep cornice.

stair_tread_m.note: T-1883: Twelve risers on 0.28 m treads, with the existing 1.2 m landing: a 4.28 m flight reaching short of the 4.44 m street line. Rounded reconstruction from the plate; the 1904 walk and footprint do not move.

stair_landing_depth_m.note: A landing one door-swing deep before the threshold.

stoop_width_m.note: T-2500: the stair beside the loggia 2.0 m wide between its cheeks, rounded down from about 2.3 m on the plan under the 1888 plate (its treads and cheeks run about 155 px at 68 px/m) so its south cheek stays clear of the bow's north end; reconstructed, as the plan is a small print.

entrance_bay.note: The register reads a north entrance on the 1888 plate; the plate is not a source record here, so the side is carried as reconstructed.

front_bays.note: Three bays across the 10.4 m front, south to north, the north bay the entrance. T-2500: the north bay stands at 8.7 m, the middle of the loggia (7.0 to 10.4 m) the 1888 plate and its plan draw, so the door at the back of the loggia and the second-storey window over the balcony are centred in it, as the plate shows the window.

front_bays_by_storey.note: T-2499: the third storey runs flat across the whole front over the bow as one arcade of six sash windows divided by colonnettes, as the plate, the mid-1950s photograph and the 1967 photograph all show it. On the plate the six lights span about 6.1 m centred on the front; set at 1.12 m centres, 6.45 m overall, the least that keeps two K01 flat lintels' horns from meeting (k01_frontage_params). The colonnettes between them are T-1883's.

side_bays.note: Four windows a storey along the south wall, west to east, the passage side.

rear_bays.note: Two windows a storey in the rear wall.

sash_by_storey.note: Double-hung sash, every clear width and height inside the contract's sash ranges ([0.75, 1.15] and [1.5, 2.4]). T-2499: the principal storey's raised to 2.4 m on a 0.9 m sill, its sills about 2.4 m over grade as the plate's are and the third storey's set to the plate's arcade lights, 0.85 m wide and 2.3 m tall (about 37 px by 100 px), sills 0.6 m over floor 3; the side and rear walls take the same rows, as they always have (nothing shows those).

basement_lights.note: Area lights under the two front windows; the basement the Sanborn 'B' records.

roof_covering.note: T-2499: a flat deck in painted flat-seam tin, the K04 library's flat-roof covering as 1634 Prairie's deck uses it, with painted tin flashing. Nothing shows it; the slate, copper rolls and valleys of the T-2293 hip went with the hip.

chimneys.note: T-2499: the same two stacks over the plan's two corner fireplaces, standing where chimney_positions puts them (inferred from the 1888 plate's plan: the library's on the south wall, the hall's on the north), now T-2302's plain capped brick prisms, which is what a K01 flat roof takes (K15's draught rule reads a hip's covering), on the K15 grouped stack's 1.155 x 0.525 m plan. Each tops out 1.4 m over the deck's high line, about 0.9 m over the front parapet, so it clears the parapet from the street as the stacks behind a flat-topped front do; neither the plate nor the later photographs show the stacks over the parapet, and their height is reconstructed. Before T-2499: T-2313: the two stacks the plan's fireplaces stand under (where each stands is chimney_positions, inferred from the 1888 plate), each built from the K15 chimney kit (T-2312) as its grouped brick stack: a 1.155 x 0.525 m common-brick shaft turned along its side wall, three flues (one a storey), two corbel courses, a stone cap, stepped side flashing, an apron below and a cricket behind, joined into the K05 roof solid so the shaft is cut where it passes through the slate and the flues are cut as dark recesses. RECONSTRUCTED: the plate's photograph is taken from the street and the house's pierced parapet hides everything behind it, so no source shows a stack above the roof. Hence no pots (the kit puts one only where a source shows it), and every size, the three flues and the 16.8 m top are the kit's. The top is the K15 draught rule on this roof: the hip's covering reaches 16.0 m within 3 m of either stack, and the cap stands 0.8 m above that, below the 17.6 m ridge. docs/LIBERTIES.md L-k15-1808-chimneys-2313.

chimney_positions.note: T-2313: where the stacks stand, read off the first-floor plan printed under the 1888 Inland Architect plate of the house. The plan draws two fireplaces in the main block, both set across a corner: the library's, in the corner where the round library meets the south wall and the music room's partition, and the hall's, against the north wall at the foot of the stair. A third, in the dining room on the rear range, stands on a range this K01 record does not build. A fireplace's flue rises in the wall behind it, and a principal room's fireplaces on the floors above stand over the one below, so each stack is placed over its fireplace's corner and set into its side wall (INFERRED, not shown: the plan is of one floor). The plan is read at its own scale, 0.0193 m to the pixel on a 3480 px scan, from the house's 10.4 m width; positions are measured from the street front, so u = 18.0 m minus the distance back from it: library 5.9 m back (u 12.1) and 0.54 m in from the south wall face; hall 4.4 m back (u 13.6) and 0.52 m in from the north wall face. Both are set 0.65 m in (v 0.65 and v 9.75): the footprint's 0.3 m margin asks at least 0.56 m, and with a stack's downhill face within a centimetre of the K05 eave box's line 0.35 m in from the wall the roof union leaves a sub-millimetre sliver at the front hip, which the K01 contract refuses. Read to about +/-0.3 m. The same plan's main block is 16.6 m deep at that scale where the record's footprint is 18.0 m; measuring from the front, which both share, keeps each fireplace's distance from the street.

window_kit.note: Every window is built from the K06 kit (T-2298): the double-hung sashes of every storey on all three glazed walls as the kit's working street sash, two lights over two, at this record's own clear sizes; the basement lights as the kit's three-light area light, without its area well, since this record sets their sills 0.35 m above grade. No source shows these sashes' glazing; two-over-two is the kit's commonest form, not a reading of this house.

entrance_kit.note: The door and its stoop are built from the K07 kit (T-2304): the kit's stone-front entrance, a four-panel leaf under a two-light transom with the dark hall behind it, in the K01 proof's own 1.20 x 2.70 m hole. T-2500 (piece 2 of T-1882) rebuilt what stands in front of it to the arrangement the Inland Architect plate of February 1888 (inland_architect_1888_02_keith_plate) and the first-floor plan printed under it draw: an open loggia at the north end of the front, a stone deck at the principal floor 2.7 m deep running from the stair to the north corner (terrace out_m; the plan draws it about 2.7 m out and 3.4 m wide on the 10.4 m front), a pedestal at each front corner (0.9 x 0.6 m, 1.0 m high, the plate's pedestal tops about 1.0 m over the deck) carrying a pair of columns side by side (2.45 m from pedestal to the top of the capital, the plate about 2.45 m), a parapet 0.9 m high between the pedestals across the front and along the north side back to the wall, the south side left open to the stair as the plan leaves it, an entablature 0.7 m deep over the columns (the plate about 0.7 m) whose top is the floor of a balcony walled by a 0.9 m parapet under the second-storey window, and a round-headed arch 1.5 m wide in the deck's face at basement level, dark behind. The stair rises on the loggia's south side, as the plate and the plan both draw it: a straight stoop 2.0 m wide centred 6.0 m from the south corner (stoop_v_m), nine equal risers of 0.167 m from the 1.2 m landing to its foot 3.60 m out, the deck's south face its north cheek as far as the deck's front, the cheek carried on from there down to the walk; the gate and the front walk line up on it. The arrangement and its proportions are read off the plate and plan at about 68 px/m on the plan and 78 px/m on the loggia's face; every dimension is rounded, and what the plate cannot give is reconstructed: the columns are plain turned shafts with a base and a swelling cap, not Ionic; the parapets and the balcony are solid stone, not the pierced balustrade and carved panel the plate shows (both are T-1883's finish); the arch's span and spring are read from a void half hidden by the stair's cheek; and the stair keeps T-2499's 1.5 m principal floor where the plate reads about 2.0 m. front_yard_m is the 1904 street grid's own distance, measured at the door square to the front, from the front face to the inner edge of Prairie Avenue's walk band (data/street_grid/1904.json face prairie__indiana_prairie_18_20: the front stands 4.44 m behind the street line and the walk begins 1 ft further out, 4.75 m). The main range has no carriage opening: the 1911 Sanborn sheet draws this lot's carriage house as the detached rear building, T-1935's. Liberty L-k07-1808-loggia-2500. T-1883 replaces the plain placeholder with paired Ionic capitals, pierced lower panels, a carved bowed balcony coping and finial piers, and concave scrolled stair cheeks. Principal floor is now 2.0 m; the column shaft/capital is 2.25 m and entablature 0.65 m, bringing the balcony floor to the unchanged second-floor datum 5.9 m. These dimensions and small carved sections are rounded reconstructions from the approved 1888 plate; the generic nine-step and solid-panel descriptions above are superseded.

windows.why_not_ordinary: The 1888 plate shows short basement lights below the raised principal floor.
The 1888 plate shows tall principal sashes including fixed transoms, rounded to 2.95 m.

bays.note: Two K08 bays (T-2308), built by generators/archetypes/k08_bays.py from data/components/prairie_1904/k08_bays.json. SOUTH FRONT BOW: the T-1837 frontage register (frontage-28-037) reads 'the south curved bay' on the Inland Architect plate of February 1888; that plate is not a source record here, so its plan, size and windows are the kit's segmental bow (3.2 m on its chord, 0.9 m out) centred 2.5 m from the south corner (0.5 m north of the front's south window axis, so its eaves clear the T-2293 downpipe at 0.35 m), two storeys from grade to under the third-floor sill, three bent sashes a storey at the house's own front sash heights, under a low copper cone. T-1882/T-1883 own the plate's actual bay and replace this one. REAR CANTED BAY: no source shows 1808's rear; a two-storey canted bay is the commonest Prairie Avenue bay (k08_bays.json), set on the rear's north window bay in the house's common brick with stone dressings, under a low tin hip. Each bay's band sits on the front's second-floor belt (5.4 m), its wall top 9.0 m, so its roof (pitch 0.25) meets the wall clear of the third-floor sill above it; the host wall carries no opening behind either. Liberty L-k08-1808-bays-2308. T-2499: the SOUTH FRONT BOW re-sized and cut down from the Inland Architect plate of February 1888 (inland_architect_1888_02_keith_plate, read in text; the bay stays reconstructed because the K08 kit, not the plate, gives its sections): the plan under the plate draws the library as a near-circle standing out of the front, read at about 22 px/m as a 5.0 m chord standing 1.2 m out, centred 3.7 m from the south corner; the photograph shows it two storeys tall, from grade to the third floor (9.8 m), capped by a curved moulded band with the third storey running flat over it, so its roof is a level cap (a K08 cone at pitch 0) under the K10 moulded_stone section carried round its plan (eaves.cornice); three principal-storey lights 0.85 x 2.4 m and four second-storey lights 0.8 x 2.2 m, as the plate draws them, the end ones held 27 and 33 degrees off the bow's axis so their recesses stay in front of the host wall (the plate's end lights stand a little wider). Before T-2499 it was the kit's 3.2 m bow under a copper cone, three lights a storey. T-1883 supersedes the south bow's smooth generic stone with the front's granite, coursed rock-face relief, three basement lights, three tall principal sashes under fixed transoms, and four second-floor sashes. The accepted bow footprint remains. Rounded course, block and transom dimensions are reconstructed from the 1888 photograph; the rear canted bay remains a declared reconstruction.

stone_front.note: The stone street wall laid as K02 coursed ashlar (T-2289): rock-faced Lemont limestone in courses, a rusticated base of two channel-jointed courses under a weathered coping whose top is the area lights' head line, quoins returning long and short on the south corner, two belts, and a flat arch of voussoirs over each opening the street_front_trim leaves a flat head (the area lights and the third floor). The kits keep what they build — the K06 sills, the K09 heads, aprons and entrance, the K07 stoop and the K08 bow — and wherever one of them is seated on the front the course under it is dressed smooth and laid flush, so no piece stands on a rock face. RECONSTRUCTED throughout: the T-1837 register reads a 'rock-faced' stone front from the Inland Architect plate of February 1888 and names no stone, so Lemont — the local quarry's limestone, the K02 library's pale coursed walling — is a working interpretation that a reading of the plate or of a specification replaces; the colour and course pattern are the library's, never the house's. The north corner is not bonded: it stands 0.02 m from Glessner's south face, closer than any rock face projects. Every course height, block length, joint, recess, arris, chip, projection, return, channel and fall is data/components/prairie_1904/k02_stone_profiles.json's, resolved by k01_frontage_params._k02 and refused outside it (docs/LIBERTIES.md L-k02-1808-stone-2289). T-1883 supersedes the Lemont working interpretation: the museum account calls this a granite front, and the approved plate shows heavy rock-faced courses. K02 granite uses the Glessner-derived rock-face approach with Keith's separate light neutral/greige load tint. Quarry and exact colour are not established by the monochrome plate; colour remains reconstructed. The fine trim is smooth dressed stone. The September 1886 Inland Architect building notice, read on printed p. 28, explicitly says granite front; neither quarry nor colour is named. T-2566: the coursing is read off the 1888 photograph (the Glessner House archive print of the plate, a18-gh-1808-keith-field-front, read at full resolution): from the basement to the third-floor line the front runs a deep rock-faced course and a thin one in turn, the deep courses about 0.5 m and the thin about 0.2 m, which the granite profile's own course_rule allows; the third storey is laid in even, much shallower-faced courses. So `coursing` lays high and low courses (low_ratio 0.4, or the profile's 0.19 m least) below 9.8 m, the high ones on the upper half of the profile's rock-face range and the low on the lower half, and even courses above with the bottom 35% of that range. The ratio and the line are measured off the print to within a course; the individual joints behind the street tree are not individually read, so the joints laid are the rhythm's, not the house's own (L-k01-keith-finish-1883).

boundary.note: T-1883: The approved 1888 photograph shows low square stone posts and solid horizontal stone rails/curbs, with an open break aligned to the stair. Replaces the generic tall iron fence, urn piers, swinging gates and unsupported south wall. Heights and sections are rounded reconstructions; the line stays on the accepted street grid. The thin iron infill in the 1965 colour photograph belongs to that later date and is not carried into 1904.

condition.note: T-2358: the house weathers to its own age on 1904-07-01 from the K14 condition kit (T-2324) rather than wearing K03's fixed full-age soot and damp. Reconstructed because every layer value is the kit's reconstruction; BUILT 1886 alone is a reading, the T-1837 building register's Cobb & Frost date that documented_range carries as inferred, so on the target date the house has stood 18 years and the kit's age factor is 0.45: damp at the wall foot and the rusticated plinth, soot under the soffit and a trail below every K06 sill and down the wall behind each downpipe, each at under half its full-age strength and scaled by the fabric (the common buff brick 1.0, the rock-faced Lemont walling 1.1, the dressed trim 1.2). Every layer's value is the kit's reconstruction (L-k14-condition-kit-2324); where an outlet's trail starts and which wall a kit piece weathers with are this ticket's (L-k14-1808-walls-2358). A dated photograph of the house would replace them. T-2359: the slate takes the kit's chimney plume leeward of the two K15 stacks at the same age, 1.35 m long and at most 0.90 at a stack's centre, read on a compass bearing through the placement's rotation (rotation_deg, resolved by the generator); the roof's plan rows and slate's full-strength response are that ticket's (L-k14-1808-roof-2359).

yard.note: The ground inside the K11 boundary, from the K14 condition kit (T-2324, data/components/prairie_1904/k14_condition.json) at the house's own age: built 1886 (this phase's documented year), so 18 years standing on 1904-07-01 and the kit's age factor 0.45. THE LINES are the boundary's and the house's: the front yard runs from the street front (and the foot of its stone bay) to the fence curb's house face, between the house's south wall line and the north lot line (s 10.225), which is all the sheet's parcel gives. THE LAWN is turf over that yard, Glessner's courtyard turf map, its surface 0.035 m over grade (the terrain under this yard rises up to 0.018 m above the lowest point the renderer beds the house on). Along the street front's wall foot and round the bay a bare strip is cut, the kit's grass_edge at 0.45: 0.14 m wide, its line wobbling 0.02 m by the property's seed. Under the stoop, an open stair whose foot alone touches grade, the ground is bare earth: no lawn is kept in its shade. THE FRONT WALK runs from the stoop's foot through the entrance pair to the public walk, 1.28 m wide between the gate piers, in flags of the stoop's own stone 0.025 m proud of the lawn, worn along its centre by the kit's front_walk path_wear (a polished line, to 0.9 at full wear). THE SERVICE WALK is cinder down the side passage, from the side gate to the house's rear corner (u 0), between the boundary wall's north face and the house's south wall, beaten along its centre by the kit's service_walk path_wear (to 0.78 at full wear, the K14 study's cinder). stone_finish.note: T-1883: The approved 1888 plate shows two staggered rows of square openings at the parapet, stone corner pinnacles, a deep diaper band and five colonnettes between the six third-storey lights. Dimensions are rounded readings against the accepted 10.4 m front; lattice bar and carving sections, rear pinnacle section and hidden deck fall are reconstructed. The front lattice ends at the corner; the north return is solid stone under a coping and a rear pinnacle, as the oblique street photographs show. The deck sits below the wall head so the lattice opens to sky. Fine foliage is represented by low relief scrolls; exact tooling is not resolved by this microfilm. Liberty L-k01-keith-finish-1883. T-2564: the north return is laid as the 1887 construction photograph and the c. 1888 view beside Glessner show it, a solid parapet and wall face of large dressed courses (about 0.46 m, read against the 1.12 m lattice) bonded with staggered joints, about 5.5 m long rather than 2.8 m (the c. 1888 view beside Glessner shows the stone return about twice the length the 2.8 m model renders from the same camera, and the 1887 construction view longer still; bounded 4.5 to 7 m, the camera fits being loose), under a rounded coping that sweeps up about 0.35 m over 0.85 m (read against the lattice in the c. 1888 view) into the corner pinnacle's base, as the front coping does at both corners; the pinnacle caps are ogival with a collar and ball finial, the rear one smaller and seated on the coping.
